title: Region colours live in the ring tool: incremental region update instead of an 8 s rebuild, neighbours always distinct
description:
User report 2026-10-04 on fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl (82 rings, 938k-triangle scan): opening the ring region tool (Ctrl+T, RingRegionTool) takes about 8 s, and the user switches back and forth between the ring tool and it only to see the region colours. Wanted: (1) the region colouring shown in the ring tool itself, as a toggleable layer, so Ctrl+T is no longer needed just to see segments; (2) region membership updated incrementally when a ring is added, moved, confirmed or deleted: only the regions that ring bounds are re-flooded, never the whole mesh; (3) neighbouring regions never get near-identical colours (today random colours collide): colour the region adjacency graph so adjacent regions differ (greedy/Welsh-Powell over a palette spread around the hue circle, cf. PATCH-4), stable across edits so colours do not reshuffle on every change. Profile the 8 s first (run-scene --profile) and name where it goes before designing the incremental path. Also make the tool's name findable: the user could not remember what Ctrl+T is called; the controls menu and status line should name it plainly.

Added 2026-10-04 from the crawfish segmentation review: 206 of the 300 regions are under 100 faces (0.08% of the area together), mostly from near-parallel rings (ring_54/ring_32, ring_65/ring_66); and 43 of the 82 rings separate nothing because the scan fused limbs to the body (main shell genus 17). While segmenting, the user needs to see both: flag sliver regions (and offer to absorb those below a size into their largest neighbour) and mark rings that do not split the region they sit in, so a ring that fails to separate a fused limb is obvious at once.

Correction 2026-10-04 to the note above: '43 rings separate nothing' overstated it. RingRegions tests each ring alone (it floods the surface with only that ring's edges as walls, RingRegions.java ~255-318): 43 of the 82 rings do not cut the surface in two on their own because the loop goes around a handle (the main shell has genus 17 from scan fusion), so they get no distal/proximal side. In the real split, with all rings as walls, they still act as walls and bound regions; whether each one ends up with different regions on its two sides was not measured. The consequence is narrower: a handle ring has no distal side of its own (which matters to anything that picks 'the distal side' of a ring), and a limb fused elsewhere needs a second cut before the limb comes free.

Profile 2026-10-04 (async-profiler cpu, run-scene --profile on a tmp copy of fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl, 938k faces, 82 rings; capture tmp/profile-open-before.html in the craw-45 worktree): Ctrl+T logged 'regions built in 8628 ms'. Of the ~965 samples under RingRegionTool.perFrame: RingRegions.flood 554 (57%) -- one whole-mesh BFS for the real split plus one more per walling ring (82) to find that ring's distal/proximal side, each going through HalfEdgeMesh accessors (faceHalfEdgeCount, halfEdgeEdge, halfEdgeTwin, IntIdList.get); RingRegions.build self 178 (18%) -- per ring a scan of all 1.4M edges plus a ringCount x ringCount x vertexCount touch test over boolean[82][469k] masks; RingRegions.sidesReached 112 (12%) -- crossing test, a full edge scan per (separating ring, other ring) pair; RingRegionTool.applyOverlay 99 (10%) -- HashMap<Integer,Integer> vertex lookup plus one boolean[vertexCount] tag mask per region (300 x 469k) handed to HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.setTags. Cause: everything is recomputed from scratch for every ring on every rebuild, and the per-ring side floods and pairwise scans scale as rings x mesh size. Plan: per-ring side data computed once per ring and cached by its mask, the real split re-flooded only inside the regions a changed ring touches, ring-ring tests restricted to the ring's own edges, and the overlay written as a per-face colour buffer rather than per-region vertex masks.
definition-of-done:
1. A profile of the 8 s on the 82-ring crawfish is on the ticket with its cause. 2. The ring tool can show region colours; adding, moving or deleting one ring updates them in well under a second on the 82-ring crawfish. 3. Adjacent regions always get clearly different colours, and colours stay put across edits. 4. The region tool is named plainly in the controls menu and status line. 5. Region results (count, membership) match the current full flood exactly on fertility and the crawfish.

6. Kept on purpose: test/benchmark/RingRegionsUpdateBenchmark prints its per-edit update times ([update] lines, the acceptance numbers for item 2), and the region layer logs one [regions] summary line per update (regions, slivers, marked rings, ms) that the user reads.
testing-plan: 1. Profile before and after on fixtures/crawfish_rings.dsl (tmp copy, never saved over). 2. Unit test: incremental update equals a full flood after a sequence of ring edits. 3. Unit test: adjacent regions' colours differ by at least a set hue/lightness distance. 4. Screenshots under tmp/.
changes-made: Region colours live in the ring tool: new RegionLayer (G toggles it in every tool, always on in the region tool) keeps RingRegions up to date incrementally. RingRegions.update re-floods only the components beside an edge whose wall changed, over flat per-face adjacency slots, and derives each ring's sides from a union-find over components instead of one whole-mesh flood per ring; results equal a fresh build (RingRegionsUpdateTest, plus RingRegionsUpdateBenchmark on the crawfish: 27 delete/add/move edits all equal). Crawfish: opening the region tool 8.6 s -> about 1 s; add one ring 37-60 ms, delete (undo) 93 ms, move 56 ms in the app (benchmark 25-127 ms). RegionColouring: adjacency-graph colouring (12-entry palette, pairwise RGB distance >= 0.45, Welsh-Powell), regions an edit did not touch keep their colour. Slivers (< 100 faces) drawn white, A absorbs them into their largest neighbour (RingRegions.absorbBelowFaces). Rings that loop a handle (43 of 82 on the crawfish, all 13 on fertility) drawn red with 'handle' beside their number; a ring with one region on both sides would read 'splits nothing' (none on either mesh). Regions draw as one range per region via HalfEdgeMeshRuntime.setFaceGroups under RingRegionTool.regionTag. Controls menu names the tools plainly (ctrl+T 'region tool: region colours, select and extract regions'); /mesh/regions reports sliver, colour, neighbours, handleRings, ringsSplittingNothing. Fertility and crawfish: region count, membership, bounding rings and problems identical to the old full flood; ring fingerprints unchanged.

Review fix 2026-10-06: RegionColouring no longer packs its own colours (hex ints with RED_SHIFT/GREEN_SHIFT/CHANNEL_MASK/CHANNEL_MAXIMUM and a hand-made Vector4f); the palette is a Color[] of ColorRGB entries (Color.YELLOW, GREEN, BLUE where exact), paletteColor(int) returns a Color via ColorRGB and toVector3f, callers use toVector4f, and SLIVER_COLOUR is Color.WHITE. Also inlined RegionLayer.wanted() (public, one caller in its own file). Region tests pass.

Review fix 2026-10-06: the palette colours are named constants in Color (REGION_COBALT, ROSE, RUST, VIOLET, MINT, AQUA, ORCHID, SAND, SPRING_GREEN, plus YELLOW, GREEN, BLUE), and a free region now takes the least used palette entry its neighbours leave free instead of the lowest, which had left nearly every region on the first four colours. On the 82-ring crawfish the 94 non-sliver regions now use all 12 entries 7-8 times each (tmp/colour-check.png); neighbours still differ and untouched regions keep their colour (RingRegionsUpdateTest, RingRegionsTest pass).
